newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr edges down in Tokyo paring overnight gains.
newsitem.headline: Dlr edges down in Tokyo paring overnight gains.

text.p: 0007 GMT --*Dollar drifts lower on profit-taking sales in early morning Tokyo, trimming overnight gains, dealers said.

*Offers from exporters and Japanese investors expected on upside, weighing on dollar/yen. But a dealer at a long-term credit bank said actual offers from investors for hedge purposes not yet detected.
*Dollar/mark's topside heavy ahead of Germany's planned statement later in day calling for strong mark and strong euro.
*But dollar's undertone still firm, with buying interest on dips intact, dealers said.

*Dealers said although they are focusing on Japanese and U.S. trade data due out later this week, impact from U.S.-Japan trade issues may be limited after series of recent comments from MOF senior official Eisuke Sakakibara.
*Sakakibara, newly appointed vice finance minister for international affairs, has repeatedly said ministry has no intention to use foreign exchange rates as trade tool.
*Japan's customs-cleared trade balance for June is due out on Thursday, while U.S. international trade data for May will be released on Friday.

*Dollar rose to 1.8040 marks in New York, its highest since August 1991, on fresh signs that Europe's proposed single currency may be weak. Meanwhile, it also edged higher towards 116 yen overnight, a level Tokyo traders have not seen since late June.
*"This is a level where market participants would like to start morning trade by selling," a city bank dealer said.

*But another city bank dealer said dollar's upward direction may be gradually confirmed as demand for dollar call options has been growing, while price for dollar put options has been going down in options market.
*In New York on Tuesday, dollar's strong rally against mark lost steam after Bundesbank council member Franz-Christoph Zeitler told reporters in Germany that dollar's rally may have become excessive.

*Zeitler added that Germany wants strong mark and German Finance Minister Theo Waigel later told Reuters the German cabinet will make a statement on Wednesday calling for a strong mark and a strong euro.
*The long-term credit bank dealer said although dollar/mark rise may be capped after such verbal intervention, some may try to test upside again to see if Germany actually intervenes.
*Dealers said 0600 GMT news conference by Bank of Japan Governor Yasuo Matsushita will have limited impact on currencies as they expect nothing new in his comments on Japan's monetary policy.
